ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, and UN Consolidated Sanctions List. Enhanced due diligence, including source-of-funds verification, is required for politically exposed persons (PEPs) per the AML/CFT Act 2012 and RMI Financial Intelligence Unit guidance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Marshall Islands Business Registry (MIBR) Online Portal, administered by the Office of the Registrar of Corporations, RMI Ministry of Finance
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be submitted exclusively in English/Latin script. No bilingual or transliterated name is recognized by the registry. The name must be distinguishable from all existing registered entities.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 14 days of a name rejection, the applicant may file a written appeal with the Registrar of Corporations providing corrective submissions, written consents for sensitive tokens, or evidence of distinguishable use. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review before the High Court of the Republic of the Marshall Islands.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for all administrative functions. A physical registered office address provided by the licensed registered agent must be maintained. Actual production facilities are not required to be located in the Marshall Islands for this low-risk non-resident manufacturing entity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 10% (low risk; no statutory license required; targeted on-site inspections may be conducted only upon specific AML/CFT suspicion or formal complaint).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act of 1990 (27 MIRC Ch. 4), as amended, particularly Sections 24-29 (Articles of Incorporation), Section 45 (Registered Office and Registered Agent), and Section 105 (Certificate of Correction)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands, Majuro
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed under the BCCA; shares may be issued with or without par value and consideration is fixed by the Board. No statutory escrow or bank deposit requirement applies to non-resident corporations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation accept and approve the subscription for its initial authorized shares upon the terms fixed by the Board; RESOLVED, that the registered office and registered agent of the Corporation established at the address approved by the Board are hereby adopted; RESOLVED, that the individuals named herein are, and each of them severally is, appointed to the offices set opposite their names until the next annual meeting, with full power to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and perfect corporate filings; RESOLVED, that the adoption of the Bylaws, the corporate seal, and the reimbursement of formation expenses are ratified; RESOLVED, that all lawful actions taken to effectuate these resolutions are approved and confirmed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a written name reservation request for the proposed corporate name (e.g., 'PlushMascot Manufacturing, Inc.') for a 60-day reservation period. The Registrar will verify the name is distinguishable from existing registered names and does not imply a government connection. Payment of the reservation fee is required before search.
required_dossiers: Corporate authorization from parent entity (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity or illegality, file a written appeal with the Registrar or re-submit a second alternative name. A consent letter from the holder of a conflicting name may cure the objection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations (submission via authorized registered agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation containing the required statutory clauses: corporate name, registered agent name and address, number of directors, share structure (classes, par value, authorized number), and permitted business purpose broad statement. Execute the Articles with a notarized acknowledgment consistent with RMI law.
required_dossiers: Consent to Appointment of Registered Agent
Consent and Acknowledgement of Initial Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a deficiency notice, file a corrected amended page via Certificate of Correction under Section 105 within 20 days; late filings incur extension fees. The statutory corporate formation is retroactive only if corrected within the cure window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing, Fee Payment, and Certificate of Incorporation Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver the executed Articles of Incorporation together with the statutory filing fee to the Registrar's counter or through an approved submission portal. Acquire the official payment receipt and record the certificate issuance date and registration number.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected, request an administrative review by the Registrar General within 14 days. Payment of a re-filing fee permits submission of a conformed Articles set.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Registered Office and Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the registered office address and registered agent designation with the Registrar. The registered agent must be a natural person or licensed entity authorized to carry on business in the Marshall Islands. Maintaining a registered agent is a continuing statutory requirement.
required_dossiers: Consent of Registered Agent to Serve
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the agent appointment is rejected, appoint an alternate registered agent within 10 days; failure results in administrative revocation of corporate existence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Adoption of Bylaws and First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation (private corporate action)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold (or act by unanimous written consent in lieu of) the first meeting of the Board. Adopt the corporate Bylaws, approve the issuance of subscribed shares, elect officers, adopt the corporate seal, authorize banking relationships, and ratify pre-incorporation expenses. Record all actions in the corporate minute book.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any resolution is irregularly adopted, rectify by unanimous written consent of all directors and shareholders; defective acts are cured by subsequent ratification under Section 110.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business License Compliance and Tax Registration (If Local Presence)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business License Office, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For a non-resident corporation with no source of income in the Marshall Islands, file an exemption notice and obtain a non-resident business acknowledgment; if a physical office or local production unit is established, apply for a Business Employment License and pay the annual license fee. No exercise of a licensed profession is implicated by plush toy manufacturing.
required_dossiers: List of officers and registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the license application is queried, provide supplemental documentation on source of income. A denial may be appealed to the Minister of Finance within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Records Book, Seal, and Share Certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Notarize and bind the Corporate Records Book containing the certificate of incorporation, bylaws, first board resolution, share ledger, stamp or seal, and share certificates. Certify the indorsement of all share certificates with the corporate seal and countersignature of the president/secretary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If share certificates are found defective, cancel and reissue under new board resolution; nil monetary penalty applies if the error is corrected before the next annual return.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Resources and Development, Republic of the Marshall Islands (industrial oversight only; no specific manufacturing permit is required for non-resident plush toy OEM operations)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Exempted - Non-Resident Business Corporation Registration; no domestic occupation or factory license is statutorily required under ISIC 3240 for offshore export-oriented plush doll production

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA), Republic of the Marshall Islands, established under the Environmental Protection Act 1984
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category III - Exempt (Registration only): ultrasonic seaming, computerized embroidery, and polyester-fiber filling do not constitute a prescribed activity; no Full EIA Report is required for low-emission, non-toxic toy assembly
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater is generated in dry assembly; any cooling water must meet RMI ambient marine discharge standards of pH 6.5-8.5 and ammonia-N below 5 mg/L. VOC emissions from adhesives (if used) must be below 50 ppm workplace limit; fibrous waste and offcuts must be bagged and disposed of in permitted landfill or exported under Basel transboundary waste rules. Sewing machine oil residues are classified as hazardous waste only if exceeding 5 kg/month.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety: unless a physical production plant is established, no civil defense license is required; if local premises exist, a Fire Safety Clearance from the RMI Fire and Rescue Authority is required for building occupancy. Structural load inspections are mandatory only for multi-story warehouses (live load 5.0 kPa). Occupational clearance requires a workplace safety self-certification covering electrical safety of sewing heads, lockout/tagout for ultrasonic welders, and ergonomic workstations; a Labor Clearance from the Marshall Islands Social Security Administration is needed if employees are hired domestically.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) Ministry of Finance, Treasury & Budget — Tax and Revenue Office (TRO), Majuro. The TRO administers the Income Tax Act and Sales Tax Act; filings are made in person at the TRO counter or through an RMI-licensed registered agent. There is no fully automated national online tax portal for offshore entities; statutory forms (Sales Tax Registration, sales tax returns, zero-rating certificates) are paper-based TRO forms.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Foreign shareholders incorporate a non-resident Business Corporation (BC) under the RMI Business Corporations Act by filing Articles of Incorporation with the RMI Registrar of Business Corporations (Ministry of Finance) and paying the incorporation fee. Step 2: Appoint and maintain an RMI-licensed registered agent and registered office; the Certificate of Incorporation is the primary corporate identity document. Step 3: No RMI TIN or income-tax registration is issued to or required from the BC because a non-resident, tax-exempt BC with no RMI-source income is outside the RMI Income Tax Act. Step 4: If the BC engages in any RMI domestic economic activity (local sales, imports, physical premises), it must apply to the TRO for a Sales Tax Registration Certificate and TIN using TRO Form S-1 (Sales Tax Registration Application) and obtain a local government Business License. Step 5: For export zero-rating purposes, the registered sales taxpayer obtains TRO approval of its export status and files returns on the TRO schedule.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone (non-resident, non-domiciled Business Corporation under the RMI Business Corporations Act: exempt from RMI income tax, withholding tax, capital gains tax, and sales tax to the extent it derives no income from sources within the RMI and conducts no taxable domestic activity; a statutory tax-exemption period, typically up to 50 years, applies to a properly structured offshore BC).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No United States-style check-the-box election and no hybrid-mismatch election is available, as the RMI imposes no income tax on tax-exempt Business Corporations. Other available statutory elections: (a) voluntary Sales Tax registration election for small traders below the mandatory threshold; (b) election to file separate or consolidated sales tax returns for multiple RMI business locations; (c) BCCA continuation/redomestication election to migrate corporate domicile into or out of the RMI while preserving the statutory tax exemption; (d) no functional-currency election is needed because the US dollar is the sole legal tender of the RMI.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Sales and Use Tax (RMI Sales Tax Act 2014, as amended)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: USD 10,000 annual gross turnover (sales and receipts) within the RMI; a person whose taxable sales/receipts exceed this threshold must register with the TRO, and persons below the threshold may register voluntarily. Imported goods are additionally subject to sales tax at the point of importation unless exempted or destined for export.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing API, or digital stamping mandate is in force. RMI operates a paper-based, self-assessment system: registered taxpayers file a simplified Sales Tax Return on a monthly/quarterly TRO schedule and retain invoices, sales slips, and export evidence in paper or electronic form. Invoices do not require TRO pre-clearance; substantiation occurs on TRO audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The 0% (zero) rate applies to taxable goods that are sold for export and are physically exported from the RMI within the contracted period (generally not exceeding 30 days after sale), and to services performed wholly outside the RMI. The claimant must be a registered sales taxpayer, must issue an invoice marked zero-rated export, and must prove that title and possession passed to an overseas customer. For the plush mascot OEM (ISIC 3240), export sales of custom plush dolls, embroidery, and ultrasonic-seaming output to offshore principals qualify for zero-rating; the burden of proving physical export rests on the exporter.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (RMI Customs Service) or approved electronic export manifest
Bill of Lading (ocean freight) or Air Waybill (air freight) issued to the overseas buyer
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank SWIFT MT103 credit advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Commercial invoice marked 'ZERO-RATED EXPORT — RMI SALES TAX ACT 2014'
Purchase order or contract confirming the offshore customer and export terms
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent zero-rating claims are treated as sales-tax evasion. The TRO may retroactively assess the uncollected 12.5% tax plus statutory monthly interest (approximately 1%–1.5% per month or part month), impose a civil fraud penalty of up to 100% of the tax evaded, and levy fines up to USD 10,000 per false document for a corporation; responsible officers may face imprisonment up to 5 years for willful evasion. The TRO may audit open years for up to 6 years (or 10 years where fraud is alleged) and claw back the zero-rating benefit, with the taxpayer bearing the burden of proving that the goods physically left RMI customs territory. TRO may also suspend or cancel the exporter's sales tax registration and zero-rating certificate.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No independent central bank exists in the Republic of the Marshall Islands; monetary oversight is exercised by the Financial Institutions Division (FID) of the RMI Ministry of Finance and the Office of the Banking Commissioner, with the United States dollar as sole legal tender and the U.S. Federal Reserve as the de facto monetary authority for currency supply.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The U.S. dollar is the national currency and the RMI maintains no exchange-control apparatus. Both current account transactions (trade, services, profit remittances) and capital account transactions (foreign direct investment, shareholder loans, repatriation of capital) are fully convertible with no prior authorization or registration requirements. Profit remittance hurdles are limited to standard AML/KYC documentation establishing beneficial ownership, source of funds, and the economic substance of the remittance instruction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender or repatriation requirement exists; because export receipts are naturally denominated in U.S. dollars, the domestic legal tender, there is no mandatory conversion ratio, no forced sale to a central bank, and no prescribed timeline for bringing export proceeds onshore.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Marshall Islands (BMI), a subsidiary of Bank of Guam
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (USD demand deposit and corporate treasury)
Capital Escrow Account / Project Development Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low domestic viability: the RMI Banking Act and Financial Transactions Reporting Act require a full banking license for deposit-taking activities, so unlicensed overseas Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) cannot open local accounts or clear through the domestic banking system. Internationally licensed EMIs may offer payment services to a non-resident RMI Business Corporation only on a non-deposit basis, but such providers generally classify an RMI non-resident entity without a U.S. or regional operating nexus as a higher compliance risk and frequently decline onboarding. The practical feasibility rating is Low to Medium, with bank-to-bank SWIFT clearing remaining the preferred channel.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: RMI-licensed banks generally require at least one director or authorized signatory to attend an in-person interview at a branch or a correspondent office during initial account opening. Remote onboarding is possible only on a case-by-case basis for low-risk non-resident corporates, subject to apostilled certified identity documents, a strong bank reference letter from a recognized financial institution, and a video-conference interview. For a plush-mascot OEM manufacturer without a local office, the compliance expectation is physical presence of a director or authorized signatory for onboarding, followed by remote ongoing banking and electronic instructions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership with tax-exempt status and no local economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Business Corporation certificate; non-resident status declaration; audited or reviewed financial statements; board resolution naming signatories; physical seat or registered agent undertaking in Majuro; detailed business plan documenting the OEM manufacturing supply chain for ISIC 3240 plush products.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear beneficial ownership or nominee shareholding structures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete beneficial ownership register filed under the RMI Financial Transactions Reporting Act; passport copies of all natural persons owning or controlling 10 percent or more; notarized declaration of trust and source-of-funds evidence where nominee layers exist.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large USD wire inflows from tax-haven or high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed OEM sales contracts with downstream customers; proforma invoices for custom plush-mascot export orders; shipping bills of lading or forwarder air waybills; customer KYC file; compliance narrative explaining the commercial purpose of each inbound wire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pre-revenue capital injection or shareholder loan without operating history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Subscription agreements, shareholder loan agreements, and intercompany funding letters; evidence of shareholder wealth and source of funds via bank statements and tax records; board resolutions formally authorizing the capital contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid payouts to unrelated beneficiaries in soft-currency jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Catalogue of approved suppliers with completed KYC status; purchase orders for embroidery thread, ultrasonic film, and polyester fiber stuffing; reconciliation of trade invoices to payment instructions; periodic compliance attestation by the designated compliance officer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing uses U.S. dollar SWIFT MT103 or MT202 transfers through the RMI bank's U.S. correspondent network. Payment narratives should reference the purpose code 'Equity subscription for working capital' or 'Intercompany shareholder loan for purchase of raw materials, ISIC 3240 plush toy production'. The beneficiary account at the RMI-licensed bank must be pre-verified, and an executed board resolution plus subscription or loan agreement must be held in the bank's compliance file to support the economic purpose of the inward remittance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement for imports of plush fabric, embroidery threads, ultrasonic film, and stuffing is executed primarily via SWIFT MT103 direct transfers for standard supplier invoices and documentary collections. Where suppliers require secured settlement, a Commercial Letter of Credit (SWIFT MT700) is issued by the RMI bank or its U.S. correspondent with payment terms at sight or deferred 30 to 60 days against presented bills of lading. Platform-based clearing (e.g., Alibaba Trade Assurance or PayPal Business) remains acceptable for small-value advances, while bank-cleared MT103 remains the primary rail for verifiable trade disbursements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/EUR and USD/JPY FX forwards with a licensed U.S.-based custodian or an RMI-licensed bank where non-USD trade payables exist
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted soft-currency settlements in certain Southeast Asian supplier currencies, booked through a group treasury entity outside the RMI
Cross-currency swaps for medium-term JPY or CNY trade payables matched against USD export receipts, executed with a major global systemically important bank under ISDA/CSA documentation
Natural offsetting via USD-denominated sourcing and cash-flow matching as a non-instrument hedge preference to minimize FX conversion requirements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual report of the business corporation (non-resident domestic corporation) confirming directors and shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before April 14 of each calendar year (first report prorated for entities incorporated after January 1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs an administrative penalty of 10% of the unpaid annual fee (minimum USD 100); continued delinquency for 90 days after the due date permits the Registrar to administratively strike the company off the register and dissolve it.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is imposed on a non-resident domestic corporation; audit is compulsory only if required by a bank, investor, shareholders' agreement, or court order.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No mandatory accounting framework is prescribed by the Business Corporations Act; IFRS, US GAAP, or other definitive national standards are acceptable where financial statements are prepared.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Registered agent conducts annual KYC verification and confirms that any shareholding transfers recorded in the Register of Members during the preceding year have been properly minute-boarded; no public UBO register is filed with the Registrar.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 – USD 1,500 per year for registered agent and registered office services in the Marshall Islands
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 – USD 10,000 for an annual certified audit performed by a Marshall Islands licensed or internationally recognized audit firm

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full income tax exemption for non-resident business corporations under Title 20 of the Marshall Islands Revised Code. No corporate income tax, capital gains tax, branch profits tax, or withholding tax on distributions to non-resident shareholders. Income sourced outside the Marshall Islands is excluded from gross revenue calculation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No corporate income tax return is required for non-resident exempt business corporations. Annual compliance is effected through the Marshall Islands Registrar of Corporations: Annual Report and Franchise Tax Remittance, filed via the online e-filing portal maintained by the Association of International Bank & Trust Companies (AIBTC) or the designated government registry portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual report must be filed and the franchise tax paid on or before the anniversary of the date of incorporation. A 30-day grace period is not automatically granted; administrative extension is available only upon prior written request to the Registrar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The exact legal name of the non-resident business corporation as stated in the Articles of Incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the registered English name exactly; no abbreviations, translations, or assumed names are permissible. Use the name as shown on the Certificate of Good Standing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name and registered physical address of the licensed Marshall Islands registered agent and the registered office within Majuro.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Marshall Islands licensed registered agent is mandatory for non-resident corporations. The registered office must be the agent's address; P.O. boxes are not acceptable as physical address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The maximum number of shares the corporation is authorised to issue and their par value or no-par status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align with the share capital table in the Articles of Incorporation; if the corporation has adopted a Memorandum of Increase, the most recently authorised capital must be reported. The franchise tax calculation depends solely on this figure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names and addresses of the current directors. A minimum of one director is required; corporate directors are permitted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Directors need not be residents of the Marshall Islands. For non-resident entities, the registered agent must hold a copy of the register of directors; filing the full register is required at incorporation, but annual returns may state the number of directors only if permitted under the BCA, subject to Registrar instructions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation of the ultimate beneficial owner(s) holding 25% or more of the issued shares; required under the Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies must maintain and file with the Registrar a beneficial ownership register containing the full legal name, date of birth, nationality, residential address, and description of the ownership interest. The data is held on a non-public government register accessible to competent authorities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the annual government franchise tax based on authorised share capital per Title 20, Section 141 of the RMC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Standard annual fee for non-resident exempt business corporations ranges from USD 400 to USD 1,500 depending on authorised shares; exemptions may apply for specially designated corporations. Confirm the applicable tier using the current fee schedule published by the Registrar.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual report attracts a fixed penalty of USD 100 and a daily surcharge of USD 10 per day of continued delinquency. Failure to pay the annual franchise tax by the due date incurs a 10% late charge and continuing accrual at the daily rate. Persistent non-compliance, defined as more than 90 days' delinquency, results in involuntary dissolution by the Registrar, loss of legal shielding, and restriction on the corporation's right to commence any action in Marshall Islands courts. Directors are additionally subject to administrative fines under the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Marshall Islands has not entered into any comprehensive double taxation agreement (DTA) that would reduce or withhold rates for dividends, interest, or royalties. Because the statutory withholding rate for non-resident shareholders is zero, no tax treaty relief protocol is required. If a foreign shareholder's home jurisdiction seeks to impose a foreign tax credit or claims a treaty benefit, the Marshall Islands competent authority (Commissioner of Internal Revenue) may issue a Certificate of Residence to confirm tax-exempt status on request, but no TRC is necessary locally to shield the distribution. Supporting evidence of corporate residence is to be maintained in the foreign jurisdiction for its own domestic purposes.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax on cross-border royalty and interest payments paid by a non-resident exempt corporation is 0%. Since the Marshall Islands does not maintain a treaty network, there is no reduced treaty rate. Payments of royalties and interest to or from a Marshall Islands exempt company are generally outside the local withholding tax administration, provided the underlying business is not conducted within the territorial limits of the Republic of the Marshall Islands.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No local transfer pricing documentation threshold exists in the Marshall Islands; transfer pricing rules have not been substantively enacted under Title 20 or the Business Corporations Act. For non-resident exempt corporations the de facto threshold is zero, meaning no local file, master file, or country-by-country report is required to be filed with the Marshall Islands tax or corporate authorities. If the corporation is the parent of a multinational group and the ultimate parent jurisdiction mandates CbC reporting, such filing occurs in that foreign jurisdiction, not in the Marshall Islands.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Marshall Islands has adopted the Economic Substance Regulations as a regional standard in response to EU/OECD anti-tax-haven pressure. The applicable doctrine applies only to resident activities considered 'relevant activities' as defined in the Economic Substance Act 2018. Contract manufacturing of plush mascots in the form of OEM stuffed toys is not a specified relevant activity, and a non-resident exempt company having no local management or employees in the Marshall Islands is outside the scope. Nevertheless, to avoid being tagged as a shell company by foreign tax administrators, the entity must demonstrate economic substance in its actual operational jurisdiction: maintain a physical presence, employees, rental contracts, and decision-making functions in the country where the plush toy manufacturing occurs.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – Misuse of Exempt Status
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a substantive management or manufacturing presence within the Republic of the Marshall Islands while continuing to claim the non-resident exemption; entering into contracts with Marshall Islands counterparties, employing local staff, or deriving gross revenue from a Marshall Islands source without obtaining a business license and filing the Gross Revenue Tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The exempt status is retroactively rescinded; the corporation becomes subject to Gross Revenue Tax at the prevailing rate of 5% on gross receipts for most businesses (banks and insurance at different rates), plus interest at 12% per annum on underpaid amounts and a negligence penalty of 20% of the understated tax. Fraudulent evasion carries an additional 50% penalty. The Registrar may strike the company from the register, and any asset transfer made to defeat tax liability is voidable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may be held jointly and severally liable for tax that the company was able to withhold, collect, and pay, where the failure is the result of wilful refusal or gross negligence. The Tax Enforcement Act permits the Commissioner of Internal Revenue to seek travel bans preventing directors from leaving the Marshall Islands, to levy attachments on personally held assets, and to institute criminal proceedings leading to imprisonment for up to five years for each count of tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Marshall Islands non-resident business corporation to hold or pass-through intellectual property, bank accounts, or contractual intangibles with no commercial rationale, no employees, and no real economic activity in the operating jurisdiction, while still claiming full pass-through status in supplier or distributor agreements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Although not sanctioned under Marshall Islands domestic law (because the Economic Substance Act does not capture a non-resident exempt company), the arrangement will be treated as a sham by foreign tax authorities. The resulting consequences include re-domestication of the entity, mandatory transparency penalties under the OECD Global Anti-Base Erosion Model Rules (Pillar 2), imposition of economic substance legislation penalties of up to USD 50,000 in the operational jurisdiction, and exchange of information pursuant to the Marshall Islands signed exchange of information arrangements with foreign tax administrations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign certificates of residency or beneficial ownership declarations that misrepresent economic activity expose themselves to a personal fine of up to USD 100,000 under the Economic Substance Act (if the entity is later deemed in scope) and to foreign enforcement actions under the common law of the operational jurisdiction. In serious cases the directors' own travel movements are subject to restrictions and asset freezes issued by foreign courts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Channeling payments received via SWIFT TT or platform-based payment rails for plush toy sales through the non-resident corporation without implementing a risk-based anti-money laundering (AML) policy, failing to identify beneficial owners of remuneration streams, or failing to file a suspicious transaction report (STR) with the Marshall Islands Financial Intelligence Unit when a transaction appears linked to money laundering or terrorism financing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Marshall Islands Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) may levy a civil penalty of up to USD 250,000 for each violation of the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Act 2012. The Minister of Finance may suspend or revoke the corporation's exemption certificate and impose a daily fine of USD 5,000 for continued non-compliance. Monetary penalties are in addition to criminal sanctions for wilful money laundering: a fine of up to USD 500,000 or the value of the laundered property (whichever is higher) and imprisonment for up to 15 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers bear primary responsibility for AML compliance. Individuals found to have knowingly participated in, facilitated, or concealed a money laundering transaction involving the plush toy corporation face personal criminal liability, including imprisonment of 10 to 15 years, forfeiture of personal and corporate assets, and prohibition from acting as a director in any Marshall Islands company. The FIU may also issue a travel ban to prevent the director from leaving the jurisdiction pending the criminal investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Maintain Beneficial Ownership Records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to identify, verify, and maintain current records of every individual who directly or indirectly owns or controls 25% or more of the corporation's shares or voting rights, particularly where the ultimate beneficiary is routed through a nominee in a foreign tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Registrar-imposed penalty of USD 10,000 for each offence under the Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations 2019. The company is given a 14-day rectification notice; continued failure results in an additional daily penalty of USD 1,000 and the Registrar may issue a 'united filing strike' resulting in dissolution. For the manufacturing group this may be cascaded by foreign registries as a negative compliance indicator, potentially triggering disqualification from public procurement and export licensing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Every director and the registered agent are jointly and severally liable for the penalty if the corporation fails to remedy the breach, and the Regulator may impose a personal penalty of up to USD 25,000 on each director and a temporary suspension of the registered agent's license. Director disqualification orders may also be issued for repeated breaches, prohibiting the director from acting in any other Marshall Islands entity for a five-year period.
